description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis) and the accuracy (ACC, %) (y-axis) for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to 10³, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, is linear and spans from 60% to 80%, with tick marks at 60, 65, 70, 75, and 80. The “Base” method (black line with circle markers) starts at approximately 61% at co-occurrence 1 and gradually increases to about 67% at 10³. “FT” (blue line with downward triangle markers) begins at ~63% and rises to ~68.5%. “IKE” (red line with upward triangle markers) starts at ~64.5% and reaches ~70%. “MEND” (brown line with diamond markers) begins at ~66.5% and climbs to ~74%. “MEMIT” (purple line with circle markers) starts at ~66.5% and increases to ~72.5%. “ROME” (green line with square markers) begins at ~72.5% and plateaus near 77.5% across the range. All methods show a general upward trend in accuracy as co-occurrence number increases, with ROME consistently achieving the highest performance and Base the lowest.
